name: Romance
definition: A developing intimate relationship becomes the central source of conflict and change, requiring reciprocal vulnerability and a satisfying decision about a shared future.
negative_signals: love interest as a minor subplot
one-sided fixation presented as mutual intimacy
diagnostic_questions: Is the relationship the story's central dramatic line?
Do both partners exercise consequential choice?

neighbors.distinction: Romance need not organize conflict through comic social disorder.
Romance centers formation or transformation of an intimate partnership.

reader_promises.name: Reciprocal centrality
reader_promises.description: Give both partners goals, boundaries, vulnerability, and power to alter the relationship.

reader_promises.name: Emotionally satisfying union
reader_promises.description: Resolve the central relationship with a credible hopeful commitment or stable togetherness.

roles.name: First partner
roles.description: Pursues intimacy while protecting a need, identity, or fear.

roles.name: Second partner
roles.description: Brings an independent objective and a different risk model for love.

roles.name: Relational pressure
roles.description: Makes incompatibility visible without replacing the partners' own choices.

stakes: Ability to love without repeating prior harm

movements.name: Meaningful connection
movements.description: Create attraction or recognition through specific interaction, not labels alone.

movements.name: Deepening intimacy
movements.description: Let trust and desire grow through reciprocal action and revealed difference.

movements.name: Relational crisis
movements.description: Make a real incompatibility or breach demand changed behavior rather than a simple explanation.

movements.name: Earned commitment
movements.description: Resolve the relationship through mutual action that addresses the central incompatibility.

complications.name: Diverging futures
complications.description: Both partners have legitimate plans that cannot continue unchanged.

complications.name: Protective secret
complications.description: A concealment meant to protect autonomy or another person damages trust.

complications.name: Power imbalance
complications.description: Status, wealth, duty, or dependence makes consent and sacrifice unequal.

twists.name: Sacrifice refused
twists.description: One partner rejects a grand gesture that would preserve unhealthy inequality.

twists.name: Obstacle internalized
twists.description: Removing the external barrier reveals a deeper behavior both must change.

conclusions.name: Shared future
conclusions.description: The partners choose a concrete workable life together.

conclusions.name: Reconciled union
conclusions.description: A separated pair rebuilds trust through demonstrated change.

conclusions.name: Hopeful beginning
conclusions.description: The story closes on credible commitment to continue building intimacy.

variation_axes.question: What must change for union to work?

subversions: Let boundary-setting become the decisive romantic act.
Make both partners change without requiring identical sacrifice.
cliches_to_avoid: Conflict sustained only by a conversation both would naturally have
Possessiveness treated as proof of love
quality_checks: Both partners have agency outside the relationship.
Intimacy grows through observable reciprocal choices.
The ending answers the practical and emotional future of the relationship.

sources.title: The Cambridge Companion to Science Fiction
sources.contribution: Summarizes the recognizable romance expectation of meeting, conflict, and love while demonstrating genre mixture.

sources.title: Making It Different: Pushing Genre Boundaries in Fantasy
sources.author_or_organization: Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association
sources.contribution: States that romance places the relationship's trials at the center while still requiring freshness.
